title: Finite rational cohomology and character filtrations for homogeneous bundles
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], with these terms as defined in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$, with $B$ a Borel subgroup, and use $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and their pairing from [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $B^-$ be the Borel opposite to $B$ relative to $T$, so its roots are $-\Phi^+$. Put $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$, $Q=\mathbf Z\Phi$, and $W=N_S(T)(F)/T(F)$, acting on $X$ by normalizer conjugation. Set $w\mathbin\cdot x=w(x+\rho)-\rho$, let $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$, and put $N=|\Phi^+|$. A rational module for any group here is an $F$-vector space with a coassociative counital coaction into its tensor product with that group's coordinate algebra; a submodule is a coaction-stable subspace. For $x\in X$, let $F_x$ be the one-dimensional $B^-$-module on which $T$ acts by $x$ and the unipotent radical acts trivially. For a finite-dimensional rational $B^-$-module $M$, let $\mathcal L(M)$ be the sheaf of sections of $S\times^{B^-}M$ on $S/B^-$: over $V\subseteq S/B^-$ its sections are regular maps $f:\pi^{-1}(V)\to M$ with $f(gb)=b^{-1}f(g)$, where $\pi:S\to S/B^-$ is the quotient. Write $H^i(M)=H^i(S/B^-,\mathcal L(M))$ for Zariski sheaf cohomology, with its natural left $S$-action, and $H^i(x)=H^i(F_x)$; set $H^i=0$ for $i<0$. Equivariance means a coaction identity, hence holds after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. A simple module is nonzero with no proper nonzero rational submodule, and a simple constituent means a simple subquotient. The homogeneous bundles above exist and $H^i(M)$ is a finite-dimensional rational $S$-module for every $i\ge0$. One has $H^i(M)=0$ for $i>N$, and a short exact sequence of finite-dimensional rational $B^-$-modules induces the natural $S$-equivariant long exact cohomology sequence. Every finite-dimensional rational $B^-$-module $M$ has a finite filtration with one-dimensional quotients $F_{x_j}$, each $x_j$ being a $T$-weight of $M$. In particular, if a simple $S$-module occurs in $H^i(M)$, it occurs in $H^i(x_j)$ for at least one character quotient of any such filtration. In degree zero the section definition identifies $H^0(x)$, equivariantly, with the actual regular-function space $\{f\in F[S]:f(gb)=x(b)^{-1}f(g),\ b\in B^-\}$. The dimension of $S/B^-$ is $N$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] to the semisimple group $S$ and the Borel $B^-$. It gives the proper finite-type quotient $Q=S/B^-$ and the faithfully flat right $B^-$-torsor $\pi:S\to Q$. The regular Noetherian geometry of this same quotient is supplied by [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-affine-cell]. The dimension clause of [lem-sfb-flag-canonical-character], applied to the Borel $B^-$, gives $\dim Q=|{-\Phi^+}|=N$ (its half-sum is $-\rho$). Thus no bound inferred merely from the number of roots is being assumed.

source.place: Theorem 17.9; Section 18c; the smooth dimension clause already recorded in flag-canonical-character

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] on $\pi$ to descend $\mathcal O_S\otimes_F M$: on $S\times_QS=S\times B^-$ the identification sends a vector over $g$ to $b^{-1}$ times it over $gb$. The identity and cocycle are $1m=m$ and $(bc)^{-1}m=c^{-1}b^{-1}m$. The descended module $\mathcal E_M$ is locally free of rank $\dim_F M$, by clause (2) of that node. The torsor is an fpqc cover: $S$ is affine of finite type, hence Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]; [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] then shows that the inverse image of an affine open of $Q$ is quasi-compact; flatness and surjectivity supply the finite affine refinement in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Compatible maps descend uniquely. A section of $\mathcal E_M$ over $V$ is therefore precisely a regular map $f:\pi^{-1}V\to M$ satisfying $f(gb)=b^{-1}f(g)$, by section descent [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent-fpqc-sections]. This identifies $\mathcal E_M$ with the specified $\mathcal L(M)$.

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent; Tag 05B2, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends; section descent Tag 03DT

proof.text: A locally free sheaf of finite rank has local affine-space bundles: on a free chart take $V\times\mathbf A^{\dim M}$; on overlaps use the invertible change-of-frame matrices. These substitutions satisfy the cocycle because the changes of bases do, so [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] gives a vector bundle. Pulled back to $S$ it is $S\times M$ with the above descent relation, hence it is the associated homogeneous bundle $S\times^{B^-}M$. The left action $a:S\times_FQ\to Q$ is the morphism which, by the Yoneda lemma, represents left translation on the fppf sheafification of $A\mapsto S(A)/B^-(A)$ that $Q$ represents by [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-affine-cell]; sheafification commutes with the product by the sheaf $S$, so $\pi$ is equivariant and identity and associativity hold as morphism equalities because they hold for $S(A)$ acting on $S(A)/B^-(A)$. Left multiplication $s(g,m)=(sg,m)$ commutes with $(g,m)b=(gb,b^{-1}m)$, so full faithfulness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent], also on $S\times Q$ and $S\times S\times Q$, descends its linearization, identity and composition. An equivariant linear map $M\to M'$ descends to a linearized sheaf map. By [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] these sheaves are quasi-coherent of finite type, and by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] they are coherent on the Noetherian scheme $Q$.

source.place: 023T and 05B2; finite local freeness and gluing; coherence uses 01XZ

proof.text: For a short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$, pullback of the descended sheaf sequence to $S$ is $\mathcal O_S\otimes_F$ that sequence. It is exact because the vector-space sequence has an $F$-linear splitting. Flat pullback is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective], so its homology sheaves pull back to zero. At a lift of each point the flat local ring map is faithfully flat by [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective]; [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-tensor-zero] makes each homology stalk zero, and [pqf-lem-sheaf-zero-stalks] makes the homology sheaves zero. Thus the descended sequence is short exact. Apply [lem-sfb-linearized-qcoherent-cohomology-coaction] to $G=S,Y=Q,\mathcal E=\mathcal L(M)$: $Q$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and separated, and the linearization was constructed above. It gives rational $S$-coactions on all $H^i(M)$ and the natural coaction-equivariant long exact sequence, including its connecting maps. This proves equivariance after every algebra extension, rather than only at $F$-points.

source.place: 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology; naturality of connecting maps in the generic linearized-cohomology input

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-coherent-hi] with $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ and the coherent $\mathcal L(M)$. A field is Noetherian, so its last clause says that $H^i(M)$ is a finite $F$-module, hence a finite-dimensional vector space. Together with Step 4 this is a finite-dimensional rational $S$-module. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] to the Noetherian scheme $Q$, its quasi-coherent $\mathcal L(M)$, and $i>N=\dim Q$; it gives $H^i(M)=0$.

The smooth connected solvable group $B^-$ embeds in an upper triangular matrix group by [lem-sfb-lie-kolchin-triangular-embedding]. Induct on $d=\dim_F M$. For $d=0$ take the empty filtration. For $d>0$, [lem-sfb-triangular-group-representation-eigenline] supplies a rational stable line $L\subset M$ with character $\chi:B^-\to\mathbf G_m$. Its restriction to the unipotent radical is trivial by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial]. Since $B^-=U^-\rtimes T$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $\chi$ is the extension of $x=\chi|_T$, and $L\simeq F_x$. Apply the induction hypothesis to the rational quotient $M/L$, whose dimension is $d-1$, and take inverse images of its filtration. This gives a finite character filtration of $M$. For any such filtration, every character quotient is a weight of $M$: lift a nonzero quotient vector to $M_j$ and decompose the lift into $T$-weight components by [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition]. In the quotient only the $x_j$-component can have nonzero image; this component belongs to $(M_j)_{x_j}\subseteq M_{x_j}$.

source.place: Theorem 16.30; Proposition 16.2(c) implies (a); Theorem 12.12; no Lie-algebra characteristic-zero theorem is used

proof.text: Fix any character filtration $0=M_0\subset\cdots\subset M_r=M$ and induct on $r$, the case $r=0$ being vacuous. Step 4 gives $H^i(M_{r-1})\to H^i(M)\to H^i(x_r)$ exact. Put $A$ equal to the first image and $C$ equal to the second image, so $0\to A\to H^i(M)\to C\to0$ is exact in rational modules. Write a simple constituent as $P/R$ for rational submodules $R\subset P\subseteq H^i(M)$. The image of $P\cap A$ in $P/R$ is either zero or all. In the second case $P/R$ is a subquotient of $A$, hence of $H^i(M_{r-1})$ by inverse images under its surjection onto $A$; induction applies. In the first case $P\cap A\subseteq R$, so $P/R$ is a quotient of $P/(P\cap A)$, which is a submodule of $C\subseteq H^i(x_r)$. Thus the constituent occurs in one of the stated $H^i(x_j)$, without assuming a cohomology filtration with those quotients.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections] to $S,T,B^-$ and the character $x\circ(B^-\to T)$. Its associated line sheaf is the same $\mathcal L(F_x)$ by the inverse-character descent relation of Step 2. It identifies $H^0(x)$ with the actual subspace of $F[S]$ satisfying $f(gb)=x(b)^{-1}f(g)$, and gives $(s f)(g)=f(s^{-1}g)$. This is the same degree-zero linearization as Step 4, hence the identification is equivariant as a coaction identity. The condition is understood on all commutative $F$-algebras, as in that node. Negative degrees are zero by convention. The zero module and the empty-root case $N=0$ are included throughout.
